primitives.name: Sample-Based Return Distribution Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model **SinkhornDRL.** Represent the return distribution by samples (no pre-specified quantiles/atoms — avoids quantile-crossing issues) and minimize the Sinkhorn divergence (entropically regularized Wasserstein distance, computed via matrix-scaling/Sinkhorn iterations) between the current and Bellman-target return distributions.

primitives.assumptions: Samples drawn from policy, finite-sample approximation valid
primitives.breakdown_regime: Sample size N must be sufficient for convergence

reasoning_traces.think:
The Sinkhorn divergence S_ε(μ, ν) bridges Wasserstein and MMD by introducing entropy regularization, which stabilizes training and improves generalization. In distributional RL, this allows modeling complex reward structures without quantile crossing. The Bellman operator T^ε_Bellman is contractive under S_ε, ensuring convergence. The use of samples instead of fixed atoms avoids quantile-crossing issues. The method's empirical success on 55 Atari games and 6 multi-dimensional settings validates its robustness. However, slower early convergence arises due to the entropy term's influence on contraction rate. This is a trade-off for improved stability and multi-dimensional support.
